137	
138	> **What actually makes `$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output` resolve is `variables.nodes[]` (step 4 below), not the instance `outputs` block.** The BPMN emitter ignores the action-node instance `outputs` block at serialization — it reads the manifest's `outputDefinition` for the activity-side mapping and reads `variables.nodes[]` for the process-level `<uipath:inputOutput>` declarations downstream nodes depend on. Authoring an `outputs` block matching the manifest is fine (the canonical examples include it for documentation), but you can skip it on action and trigger nodes. **Exception — Orchestrator-job nodes** (api-workflow, rpa-workflow, agent, agentic-process, function): the converter DOES read their instance `outputs` and copies each `source` verbatim into `model.outputDefinition`, so a wrong `source` there (e.g. `=result.response`) breaks the downstream variable. Declare `error` only and let `output` be injected. End / terminate nodes are different — see [end/impl.md](plugins/end/impl.md). The standard patterns are in [file-format.md — Node outputs](../../shared/file-format.md#node-outputs). **Always run `uip maestro flow format` after structural edits — it regenerates `variables.nodes[]` from the current node graph (MST-9972).**
139	
140	> **No instance `model` block.** BPMN type, serviceType, event definition, and binding/context templates are provided by the definition in `definitions[]` (copied verbatim from the registry). Instance-specific identity fields live under `inputs`: `entryPointId`/`isDefaultEntryPoint` for triggers, `color`/`content` for sticky notes, and `source` for every inline-agent-related node — `uipath.agent.autonomous` plus every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) writes the inline agent's `projectId` (autonomous) or resource UUID (resource nodes) at `inputs.source`. Their definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists source identity onto the instance — no `"model": { "source": ... }` block is written. See [file-format.md — Instance-specific identity fields](../../shared/file-format.md#instance-specific-identity-fields).
141	
142	> **No `ui` block on nodes.** Do NOT put `position`, `size`, or `collapsed` on the node. Add a layout entry instead (step 5).
143	
144	3. Add the definition to `definitions` (if this type is not already present):
145	   - Paste the returned node definition object from the registry response
146	   - Set the node instance `typeVersion` to the pasted definition's exact `version`
147	   - One definition per unique `type:typeVersion` — not one per node instance
148	
149	> **Resource nodes — extra step.** If the node type is one of `uipath.core.rpa-workflow.*`, `uipath.core.agent.*`, `uipath.core.flow.*`, `uipath.core.agentic-process.*`, `uipath.core.api-workflow.*`, or `uipath.core.human-task.*`:
150	> 1. The instance stays minimal — just `inputs`/`outputs`/`display`.
151	> 2. Add matching entries to the top-level `bindings[]` array (sibling of `nodes`/`edges`/`definitions`): two entries per resource (`name` + `folderPath`) with `resourceKey` exactly matching the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey`.
152	>
153	> The BPMN emit layer rewrites the definition's `<bindings.{name}>` placeholders to `=bindings.{id}` by matching on `(resourceKey, name)`. Without matching entries in top-level `bindings[]`, `uip maestro flow validate` passes but `uip maestro flow debug` fails with "Folder does not exist or the user does not have access to the folder." The definition stays verbatim from the registry — do NOT rewrite `<bindings.*>` placeholders inside it. See the relevant plugin's `impl.md` for the exact JSON.
154	
155	4. Add node output variables to `variables.nodes` (REQUIRED — the BPMN emitter reads this to declare process-level variables. `uip maestro flow format` regenerates this block from `nodes[]` + `definitions[]`, so running format after edits will self-heal an omitted entry; running validate alone does not. Without it, downstream `$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output` resolves to `undefined` at runtime — MST-9972):
156	
157	```json
158	[
159	  {
160	    "id": "<NODE_ID>.output",
161	    "type": "object",
162	    "description": "<Output description>",
163	    "binding": {
164	      "nodeId": "<NODE_ID>",
165	      "outputId": "output"
166	    }
167	  },
168	  {
169	    "id": "<NODE_ID>.error",
170	    "type": "object",
171	    "description": "Error information if the node fails",
172	    "binding": {
173	      "nodeId": "<NODE_ID>",
174	      "outputId": "error"
175	    }
176	  }
177	]
178	```
179	
180	5. Add a placeholder layout entry for the node in the top-level `layout.nodes` object — `flow format` rewrites both `position` and `size` on save:
181	
182	```json
183	"layout": {
184	  "nodes": {
185	    "<UNIQUE_NODE_ID>": {
186	      "position": { "x": 0, "y": 0 },
187	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
188	      "collapsed": false
189	    }
190	  }
191	}
192	```
193	
194	**Layout rule:** Don't compute coordinates by hand — run `uip maestro flow format <ProjectName>.flow` after edits. Format arranges nodes horizontally, sets each node's size by its canvas shape (inline agents → 288×96, containers → 560×320, everything else → 96×96), and recurses into subflows.
195	
196	### Delete a node
197	
198	**Tool:** `Edit` (remove from `nodes[]` + dependent edges + orphaned definitions + `variables.nodes` + `variableUpdates`), or `scripts/flow_edit.py delete-node --flow <ProjectName>.flow --id <NODE_ID>`, which performs the whole cascade below and reports what it removed. It leaves `bindings_v2.json` alone and prints the reminder in step 6, because that decision depends on the other connector nodes.
199	
200	1. Use `Edit` to remove the node object from `nodes`
201	2. Remove **all edges** where `sourceNodeId` or `targetNodeId` equals the node's `id`
202	3. If no other node uses the same `type`, remove the definition from `definitions`
203	4. Remove the node's entry from `variables.nodes`
204	5. Remove any `variableUpdates` entries keyed by the node's `id`
205	6. If the node is a connector node, remove its binding from `bindings_v2.json` **only if no other node in the flow uses the same connector**. Bindings are shared at the connector level (keyed by `metadata.Connector`), not per node.
206	
207	### Add an edge
208	
209	**Tool:** `Edit` (insert into `edges[]` with `targetPort`), or:
210	
211	```bash
212	python3 scripts/flow_edit.py add-edge --flow <ProjectName>.flow \
213	    --source <SOURCE_NODE_ID> --source-port <SOURCE_PORT> \
214	    --target <TARGET_NODE_ID> --target-port <TARGET_PORT>
215	```
216	
217	It derives the `id` pattern below, requires both ports, verifies both nodes exist, and sets `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true` on the source when `--source-port error` is used.
218	
219	Use `Edit` to add an edge object to the `edges` array:
220	
221	```json
222	{
223	  "id": "edge_<SOURCE_NODE_ID>_<SOURCE_PORT>_<TARGET_NODE_ID>_<TARGET_PORT>",
224	  "sourceNodeId": "<SOURCE_NODE_ID>",
225	  "sourcePort": "<SOURCE_PORT>",
226	  "targetNodeId": "<TARGET_NODE_ID>",
227	  "targetPort": "<TARGET_PORT>"
228	}
229	```
230	
231	**Critical:** the edge `id` MUST match the pattern above — never a bare UUID or any id starting with a digit.
232	
233	**Critical:** `targetPort` is required on every edge. Omitting it produces a validation error.
234	
235	**Critical:** the outgoing port field is named `sourcePort`, not `sourceHandle`. `sourceHandle` is a UI/runtime term, not valid `.flow` JSON.
236	
237	**Critical:** for `sourcePort: "error"`, also set `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true` on the source node. Without the flag, Studio Web hides the source handle and `uip maestro flow validate` fails. The converse is equally strict: **never set the flag on a node that has no `error` edge** — it suppresses the node's fault and the run reports success while the work failed. See [file-format.md — Default: off](../../shared/file-format.md#default-off--enable-only-for-a-failure-the-flow-actually-handles).
238	
239	**Edge ID:** `edge_<SOURCE_NODE_ID>_<SOURCE_PORT>_<TARGET_NODE_ID>_<TARGET_PORT>`.
240	
241	See each plugin's `planning.md` or [file-format.md — Standard ports](../../shared/file-format.md) for port names by node type.
242	
243	### Delete an edge
244	
245	**Tool:** `Edit`
246	
247	Use `Edit` to remove the edge object from the `edges` array by its `id`.
248	
249	### Update node inputs
250	
251	**Tool:** `Edit` (in-place value tweak — preserves node ID and `$vars`)
252	
253	Use `Edit` to modify the `inputs` object of the target node in-place. No need to delete and re-add.
254	
255	```json
256	{
257	  "id": "checkStatus",
258	  "type": "core.logic.decision",
259	  "inputs": {
260	    "expression": "$vars.fetchData.output.statusCode === 200"
261	  }
262	}
263	```
264	
265	This is a key advantage of `Edit` — input updates are a single field edit, not the delete + re-add pattern required by the CLI.
266	
267	---
268	
269	## Variable Operations
270	
271	These are `Edit`-only — the CLI does not support variable management. There is no fallback strategy. `scripts/flow_edit.py add-variable | add-output-mapping | add-variable-update` writes the three shapes below (it refuses a `variableUpdates` entry for a variable that is not `inout`, and refuses an output mapping on a node that is not End/terminate).
272	
273	### Add a workflow variable
274	
275	**Tool:** `Edit`
276	
277	Use `Edit` to add an entry to `variables.globals`:
278	
279	```json
280	{
281	  "id": "<VARIABLE_ID>",
282	  "direction": "in|out|inout",
283	  "type": "string|number|boolean|object|array|file",
284	  "defaultValue": "<OPTIONAL_DEFAULT>",
285	  "description": "<OPTIONAL_DESCRIPTION>"
286	}
287	```
288	
289	For `out` variables: add output mapping to **every reachable End node** (see below).
290	For `inout` variables: add `variableUpdates` entries on nodes that modify the state.
291	Attachment-carrying inputs MUST use `"type": "file"` — `"object"` breaks attachment binding and faults IxP extraction with `[430002]` (see [plugins/ixp/impl.md#debug](plugins/ixp/impl.md#debug)).
292	
293	See [variables-and-expressions.md](../../shared/variables-and-expressions.md) for the full schema, type system, and scoping rules.
294	
295	### Add output mapping on an End node
296	
297	**Tool:** `Edit`
298

1	# Flow Editing Operations — CLI Carve-Outs
2	
3	This is **not** a structural editing guide. Use direct `.flow` authoring via [editing-operations-json.md](editing-operations-json.md) for OOTB node/edge/variable CRUD, trigger swaps, output mapping, subflows, inline-agent node/wiring, non-connector resources, and in-place updates.
4	
5	> **When to use this file:** only for CLI-managed carve-outs documented by a plugin: connector activities, connector triggers, and managed HTTP nodes (both `node add` and `node configure`). If you landed here while adding/removing/wiring OOTB nodes, inline-agent nodes, non-connector resources, or other structural graph elements, go back to the Edit / Write guide.
6	
7	The primitive commands below are support commands for carve-out workflows only. They are not an opt-in path for non-carve-out structural edits.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## Primitive Commands for Carve-Out Workflows
12	
13	### Add a node
14	
15	```bash
16	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow <node-type> --output json \
17	  --input '<INPUT_JSON>' \
18	  --label "<LABEL>" \
19	  --position <X>,<Y> \
20	  --parent <PARENT_NODE_ID>
21	```
22	
23	**What the CLI handles automatically:**
24	- Inserts node into `nodes` array with a generated `id`
25	- Copies the definition from the local registry cache into `definitions` (one per unique type)
26	- Adds node output variables to `variables.nodes`
27	
28	**Flags:**
29	
30	| Flag | Required | Description |
31	|------|----------|-------------|
32	| `--input` | No | JSON object of node-specific inputs (expression, script, URL, etc.). Omit for nodes with no inputs (merge, end, terminate). |
33	| `--label` | No | Display label shown on the canvas |
34	| `--position` | No | `x,y` coordinates. Any value is fine (e.g. `0,0`) — `flow format` rewrites positions on save. |
35	| `--parent` | No | ID of an existing container node (e.g. a `core.logic.loop`). Sets `parentId` on the new node, placing it inside that container. Required for every node in a loop body — see [loop/impl.md](plugins/loop/impl.md). |
36	| `--output json` | Yes (for parsing) | Structured JSON response with the assigned node `id` |
37	
38	**Shell quoting tip:** If `--input` JSON contains special characters (quotes, braces, `$vars`), write it to a temp file and pass `--input "$(cat /tmp/input.json)"`.
39	
40	### Remove a node
41	
42	```bash
43	uip maestro flow node remove <ProjectName>.flow <NODE_ID>
44	uip maestro flow node remove <ProjectName>.flow <NODE_ID> --output json
45	```
46	
47	**What the CLI handles automatically:**
48	- Removes the node from `nodes`
49	- Removes all connected edges
50	- Removes orphaned definitions (definitions no longer referenced by any node)
51	- Removes orphaned bindings (connector bindings are shared at the connector level — a binding is only orphaned when no remaining node uses that connector)
52	- Removes node variables from `variables.nodes`
53	
54	### List nodes
55	
56	```bash
57	uip maestro flow node list <ProjectName>.flow --output json
58	```
59	
60	Returns all nodes with their `id`, `type`, and `display.label`. Use this to discover node IDs before wiring edges or removing nodes.
61	
62	### Add an edge
63	
64	```bash
65	uip maestro flow edge add <ProjectName>.flow <SOURCE_NODE_ID> <TARGET_NODE_ID> --output json \
66	  --source-port <PORT> \
67	  --target-port <PORT>
68	```
69	
70	**What the CLI handles automatically:**
71	- Inserts edge into `edges` array with a generated `id`
72	- Sets `targetPort` (required — validate rejects edges without it)
73	
74	See each plugin's `planning.md` or [file-format.md — Standard ports](../../shared/file-format.md) for port names by node type.
75	
76	### Remove an edge
77	
78	```bash
79	uip maestro flow edge remove <ProjectName>.flow <EDGE_ID>
80	uip maestro flow edge remove <ProjectName>.flow <EDGE_ID> --output json
81	```
82	
83	### List edges
84	
85	```bash
86	uip maestro flow edge list <ProjectName>.flow --output json
87	```
88	
89	Returns all edges with `id`, `sourceNodeId`, `sourcePort`, `targetNodeId`, `targetPort`.
90	
91	### Configure a connector node
92	
93	After adding a connector node with `node add`, configure it with connection details:
94	
95	```bash
96	uip maestro flow node configure <ProjectName>.flow <NODE_ID> \
97	  --detail '<DETAIL_JSON>'
98	```
99	
100	**What the CLI handles automatically:**
101	- Populates `inputs.detail` (connectionId, method, endpoint, bodyParameters, etc.)
102	- Creates connection binding entries in `bindings_v2.json`
103	- Creates connection resource files under `resources/solution_folder/connection/`
104	
105	The `--detail` JSON schema differs between connector activity nodes, connector trigger nodes, and managed HTTP nodes — see [connector/impl.md](plugins/connector/impl.md), [connector-trigger/impl.md](plugins/connector-trigger/impl.md), and [http/impl.md](plugins/http/impl.md) for the exact fields.
106	
107	**Shell quoting tip:** For complex `--detail` JSON, write it to a temp file:
108	
109	```bash
110	uip maestro flow node configure <file> <nodeId> --detail "$(cat /tmp/detail.json)" --output json
111	```
112	
113	### Configure a managed HTTP node
114	
115	After adding a `core.action.http.v2` node, configure it with target connector and connection details:
116	
117	```bash
118	uip maestro flow node configure <ProjectName>.flow <NODE_ID> \
119	  --detail '{
120	    "authentication": "connector",
121	    "targetConnector": "<TARGET_CONNECTOR_KEY>",
122	    "connectionId": "<TARGET_CONNECTION_ID>",
123	    "folderKey": "<FOLDER_KEY>",
124	    "method": "GET",
125	    "path": "/api/endpoint",
126	    "query": {"param1": "value1"}
127	  }'
128	```
129	
130	**What the CLI handles automatically:**
131	- Wraps your fields into the full `inputs.detail` structure (connector: `uipath-uipath-http`, bodyParameters, configuration)
132	- Generates `bindings_v2.json` with the target connector's connection
133	- Creates a connection resource file under `resources/solution_folder/connection/`
134	
135	See [http/impl.md](plugins/http/impl.md) for the full configuration workflow and JSON structure.
136	
137	### Validate
138	
139	```bash
140	uip maestro flow validate <ProjectName>.flow --output json
141	```
142	
143	Run **once** after all nodes, edges, and configuration are complete. Do not validate after each individual edit — intermediate states are expected to be invalid.
144	
145	---
146	
147	## Carve-Out Composite Operations
148	
149	These combine primitives only for workflows that are themselves carve-outs. Do not use them for non-carve-out structural edits; use [editing-operations-json.md](editing-operations-json.md) instead.
150	
151	### Replace manual trigger with connector trigger
152	
153	1. Remove the manual trigger (also removes its edges and orphaned definition):
154	   ```bash
155	   uip maestro flow node remove <ProjectName>.flow start --output json
156	   ```
157	2. Add the connector trigger node:
158	   ```bash
159	   uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow <TRIGGER_NODE_TYPE> \
160	     --label "<LABEL>" --position 200,144 --output json
161	   ```
162	3. Re-wire edge from the new trigger to the next node:
163	   ```bash
164	   uip maestro flow edge add <ProjectName>.flow <NEW_TRIGGER_ID> <NEXT_NODE_ID> \
165	     --source-port output --target-port input --output json
166	   ```
167	4. Configure the trigger with connection and event parameters:
168	   ```bash
169	   uip maestro flow node configure <ProjectName>.flow <NEW_TRIGGER_ID> --detail '<TRIGGER_DETAIL_JSON>'
170	   ```
171	
172	See [connector-trigger/impl.md](plugins/connector-trigger/impl.md) for the full `--detail` schema.
173	
174	---
175	
176	## Operations Not Supported by CLI
177	
178	These operations require the `Edit` tool. Use the [Edit / Write strategy guide](editing-operations-json.md) for:
179	
180	1. **Any non-carve-out structural edit** — node/edge CRUD, scheduled triggers, HITL QuickForm nodes, inline-agent nodes, non-connector resources, and graph rewiring
181	2. **Node input updates** — the CLI does not have a `node update` command; use `Edit` to preserve node IDs and `$vars.{nodeId}` references
182	3. **Workflow variables** — add/remove/update `variables.globals`
183	4. **Variable updates** — add/modify `variables.variableUpdates` entries
184	5. **Output mapping on End nodes** — add `outputs` object with `source` expressions
185	6. **Subflows** — create `subflows.{nodeId}` with nested nodes, edges, variables
186

1	# HTTP Request Node — Manual Mode
2	
3	Use this walkthrough when there is no IS connector for the target service, the API needs no auth (or auth you pass yourself in headers), or you are prototyping against an arbitrary REST endpoint. For connector-managed auth, use [impl-connector.md](impl-connector.md) instead.
4	
5	**No connection lookup required.** Manual mode uses `ImplicitConnection` — there are no IS bindings.
6	
7	Before starting, read [impl.md](impl.md) for the node type, registry validation, and the "always use `node configure`" rule. Follow Steps 1–4 in order.
8	
9	## Step 1 — Add the node
10	
11	```bash
12	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow core.action.http.v2 \
13	  --label "<HTTP node label>" --output json
14	```
15	
16	> **Inside a loop body?** Add `--parent <LOOP_NODE_ID>` to set `parentId`. Without it, the node runs outside the loop context and outputs are null. See [loop/impl.md](../loop/impl.md).
17	
18	The CLI copies the manifest into `definitions[]`, adds the node instance, registers `variables.nodes`, and inserts a `layout.nodes` placeholder — byte-for-byte from the registry. Save the returned `<nodeId>` — Step 2 reuses it. Leave `inputs` empty; Step 2 populates `inputs.detail`. Do not hand-author the definition — see [impl.md — Add the node](impl.md#add-the-node).
19	
20	## Step 2 — Configure the node
21	
22	> **Find missing values first.** Before composing `url` / `query` / `body`, resolve any values the agent doesn't have (IDs from names, required body fields, response shape, …). See [/uipath:uipath-platform — http-request.md](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/http-request.md).
23	
24	```bash
25	uip maestro flow node configure <ProjectName>.flow <nodeId> \
26	  --detail '{
27	    "authentication": "manual",
28	    "method": "GET",
29	    "url": "https://api.example.com/endpoint",
30	    "query": {"param1": "value1"}
31	  }' --output json
32	```
33	
34	The CLI:
35	
36	- Builds the full `inputs.detail` (manual auth, `ImplicitConnection`, bodyParameters, essentialConfiguration)
37	- Does **not** generate `bindings_v2.json` or a connection resource file — manual mode needs neither
38	
39	`url` must be a full URL (scheme + host + path). For auth headers you control, pass them under `headers`:
40	
41	```bash
42	uip maestro flow node configure <ProjectName>.flow <nodeId> \
43	  --detail '{
44	    "authentication": "manual",
45	    "method": "GET",
46	    "url": "https://api.example.com/me",
47	    "headers": {"Authorization": "=js:`Bearer ${$vars.apiToken}`"}
48	  }' --output json
49	```
50	
51	**Dynamic values:** HTTP input fields do not resolve `{$vars.x}` brace-templates — use `=js:` expressions for any dynamic `url` / `headers` / `body` / `query`. Pass the `=js:` string verbatim in `--detail`. Full rationale and examples: [impl.md — Dynamic values](impl.md#dynamic-values-in-url--headers--body--query).
52	
53	## Step 3 — (Optional) Response branches
54	
55	Skip unless you need to route downstream paths based on response content (e.g., `items.length > 0` vs empty). For generic call-failure handling use the `error` port in Step 4 instead. Full syntax and rules: [impl.md — Conditional branches](impl.md#conditional-branches).
56	
57	## Step 4 — Wire edges
58	
59	The HTTP node's target port is `input`. Source ports: `default` (success), `error` (network/non-2xx), `branch-{id}` (one per Step 3 entry). Wire `default` to the next node. Wire `error` to a handler **only when the requirements say what a failed call should do** — with no `error` edge the call faults the flow, which is the correct default, and setting `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true` without the edge swallows the failure into a run that reports success. See [file-format.md — Default: off](../../../../shared/file-format.md#default-off--enable-only-for-a-failure-the-flow-actually-handles).
60	
61	Edge JSON shapes and all four examples (upstream→node, default→downstream, error→handler, branch→downstream): [impl.md — Wire edges](impl.md#wire-edges).
62	
63	## Debug
64	
65	See [impl.md — Debug](impl.md#debug). For manual mode, watch for `ImplicitConnection` errors — they signal a missing `authentication: "manual"` flag or a non-URL `url` value.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""DriveToSlack: structural and runtime checks for the cross-connector flow.
3	
4	Runs every check in sequence. Exits non-zero on the first failure with a
5	``FAIL: ...`` message; prints ``OK: ...`` per check and a final summary on
6	success.
7	
8	Checks performed:
9	  1. Flow file exists and is valid JSON with ``nodes`` and ``edges``.
10	  2. Flow references the ``uipath-google-drive`` connector.
11	  3. Flow references the ``uipath-salesforce-slack`` connector.
12	  4. Flow references the Slack "Send File to channel" operation.
13	  5. Slack node references a Google Drive node id (data binding wired).
14	"""
15	
16	from __future__ import annotations
17	
18	import glob
19	import json
20	import re
21	import sys
22	
23	FLOW_GLOB = "**/DriveToSlackTest*.flow"
24	DRIVE_KEY = "uipath-google-drive"
25	SLACK_KEY = "uipath-salesforce-slack"
26	
27	
28	def _fail(msg: str) -> None:
29	    sys.exit(f"FAIL: {msg}")
30	
31	
32	def _flow_path() -> str:
33	    flows = glob.glob(FLOW_GLOB, recursive=True)
34	    if not flows:
35	        _fail(f"No flow file matching {FLOW_GLOB}")
36	    return flows[0]
37	
38	
39	def main() -> None:
40	    path = _flow_path()
41	    raw = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
42	    try:
43	        flow = json.loads(raw)
44	    except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
45	        _fail(f"{path} is not valid JSON: {e}")
46	
47	    if "nodes" not in flow or "edges" not in flow:
48	        _fail("Flow missing 'nodes' or 'edges'")
49	    print(f"OK: {len(flow['nodes'])} nodes, {len(flow['edges'])} edges")
50	
51	    if DRIVE_KEY not in raw:
52	        _fail(f"{DRIVE_KEY} connector key not found")
53	    print(f"OK: {DRIVE_KEY} connector key present")
54	
55	    if SLACK_KEY not in raw:
56	        _fail(f"{SLACK_KEY} connector key not found")
57	    print(f"OK: {SLACK_KEY} connector key present")
58	
59	    if not re.search(r"send[\s_-]?file[\s_-]?to[\s_-]?channel", raw.lower()):
60	        _fail("Send File to channel operation not referenced")
61	    print("OK: Send File to channel operation present")
62	
63	    drive_nodes = [n for n in flow["nodes"] if DRIVE_KEY in json.dumps(n)]
64	    slack_nodes = [n for n in flow["nodes"] if SLACK_KEY in json.dumps(n)]
65	    if not drive_nodes or not slack_nodes:
66	        _fail("Missing drive or slack node")
67	    drive_ids = {n.get("id") for n in drive_nodes if n.get("id")}
68	    slack_blob = json.dumps(slack_nodes)
69	    if not any(did in slack_blob for did in drive_ids):
70	        _fail("Slack node does not reference Google Drive node id (no data binding)")
71	    print("OK: Slack node references Google Drive node output")
72	
73	    print("OK: all DriveToSlack checks passed")
74	
75	
76	if __name__ == "__main__":
77	    main()

    timeout: 60
    expected_exit_code: 0
    weight: 3.0
    pass_threshold: 1.0

  - type: run_command

    expected_exit_code: 0
    weight: 1.0
    pass_threshold: 0

\

  && cd "VendorInvoiceProcessing" \
  && uip maestro flow init "VendorInvoiceProcessing" --output json \

  && uip maestro flow node remove "VendorInvoiceProcessing.flow" start --output json \
  && uip maestro flow node add "VendorInvoiceProcessing.flow" "uipath.connector.trigger.uipath-microsoft-onedrive.file-created" --label "New Vendor Invoice File Created" --position 0,144 --output json \
  && uip maestro flow node add "VendorInvoiceProcessing.flow" "uipath.connector.uipath-microsoft-onedrive.download-file" --label "Download Invoice File" --position 200,144 --output json \
  && uip maestro flow node add "VendorInvoiceProcessing.flow" "core.action.http.v2" --label "POST Invoice Data to SAP" --output json
parameters.description: Scaffold solution + flow project, remove manual trigger, add connector trigger + download-file + HTTP nodes
